subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lucas Perez <lucas.perez@atlas-payments.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments

Thanks for the call this morning — good alignment on the core use case (real-time fraud scoring for checkout flows). Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the proposed POC scope and success criteria so we have something to review internally and with the Atlas team. Please see the summary below and let me know if I missed anything.

POC scope (2 weeks):
- Integrate Redwood inference endpoint with 1 checkout flow (web)
- Validate latency/throughput under production-like traffic (synth load)
- Evaluate cost per resolved transaction & quality of fraud predictions

Proposed success criteria / KPIs to validate:
- Latency: median tail (p95) for single-request scoring <= 150ms (under 30 TPS steady-state)
- Throughput: sustain bursts to 100 TPS with graceful degradation and autoscaling behavior
- Cost: average cost/token and cost per transaction estimate (target < $0.002 per scored txn based on current model)
- Quality: parity or improvement vs current baseline (AUC lift >= 0.02 or false positive reduction >= 10%)
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% and no more than one incident requiring rollback during the POC

Ownership / next steps:
- Atlas: provide sample traffic profile + test accounts (Maya/Lucas)
- Redwood: provide integration checklist, POC config, monitoring dashboard, and a small test harness (Jordan / Lauren)
- Timeline: start integration week of Apr 19; run tests Apr 26-30; final review week of May 3

Attachments: POC-MAP-2027-04-10.pdf (draft mutual action plan), redwood-kpi-template.xlsx (KPI tracking template)

Thanks — I can hop on a quick follow-up with your infra team if helpful.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Lucas Perez <lucas.perez@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@atlas-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments

Thanks Jordan — this looks great and captures what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: Our checkout SLA is 200ms p95 end-to-end, but the scoring component ideally should be <= 120ms p95 to leave headroom for other services. Can Redwood hit 120ms p95 in your experience?
- Throughput: 100 TPS peak is accurate for the busiest checkout window, but average will be around 15-20 TPS.
- Quality: we have an internal model baseline with AUC=0.78; target of +0.02 makes sense.

We can provide a 48-hour sample of production-like traffic and a test account by Apr 16. Also, happy to have our infra lead on a call next week to align on network/integration.

Maya and I are aligned to start the integration Apr 19.

—Lucas
Lucas Perez
Head of Risk Engineering | Atlas Payments
lucas.perez@atlas-payments.com

Looping in Markus (runtime lead) to confirm feasibility on the 120ms p95 target and autoscaling plan. Markus — can your team run a quick perf sweep with the model variant Lucas will share and confirm expected p95 at 20 TPS and at 100 TPS with our continuous batching enabled? Also will provide an estimate for cost/token for both baseline and quantized variants.

Action items I will own:
- Draft the test plan and monitoring dashboard (use redwood-kpi-template.xlsx) — due Apr 16
- Set up a temporary Dedicated test pool for the POC; estimate of costs before integration — due Apr 18

Jordan — I’ll sync with you after Markus completes the perf sweep to finalize the MOP and kickoff timings.

Thanks,
Lauren

lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Lucas Perez <lucas.perez@atlas-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments

Quick update after an initial sweep against a similar model and a synthetic traffic profile: 
- At 20 TPS steady-state we see p95 ~ 90-110ms depending on sequence length; with our KV/prefix caching this should be stable.
- At 100 TPS burst using continuous batching and 2x workers we can sustain ~130-160ms p95; we’ll instrument graceful queueing to keep error rate <0.5% and enable autoscale triggers on queue depth.
- Cost estimates: baseline model ~ $0.0025 per scored txn; quantized variant ~ $0.0016 per scored txn (need to validate quality tradeoffs).

Next steps: Markus to run a perf job with Atlas sample traffic once provided (Maya/Lucas) and share full dashboard (Grafana link) by Apr 18. If the p95 at 100 TPS is consistently >150ms we’ll propose a hybrid fallback (smaller model variant for bursts) to meet SLA.

-Markus
